items.title: Positive rescaling of an upper-strip W*-KMS flow
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let
$M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a nonzero unital $*$-subalgebra with $M=M''$,
where $\mathcal B(H)$ is the bounded-operator algebra and $M'$ is its
commutant. Let $\omega$ be a normal state, meaning a bounded positive linear
functional with $\omega(I)=1$ that preserves suprema of bounded increasing
nets of positive elements. Let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a one-parameter group
of bijective unital $*$-automorphisms of $M$, with dimensionless parameter
$t$, such that $t\mapsto\varphi(\alpha_t(X))$ is continuous for every
$X\in M$ and every normal linear functional $\varphi$ on $M$ (an element of
the predual). Suppose
that for some dimensionless $\theta>0$, for every $A,B\in M$ there is a
bounded continuous function $F_{A,B}$ on
$S_\theta=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le\theta\}$, holomorphic
inside, with
$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+i\theta)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A).$$
This is the upper-strip convention of the preceding von Neumann KMS
definition. For any scalar $\lambda>0$, set
$\widetilde\alpha_\tau=\alpha_{\tau/\lambda}$ for $\tau\in\mathbb R$.
Then $\widetilde\alpha$ is again a point-ultraweakly continuous
one-parameter group, and $\omega$ satisfies the same upper-strip boundary
condition for $\widetilde\alpha$ on the strip of width $\lambda\theta$.

references.title: F. Hiai, Concise lectures on selected topics of von Neumann algebras, arXiv:2004.02383
references.locator: Complete 159-page lecture notes; §2.2, Definition 2.11 and Theorem 2.14 (PDF pp. 17–19), for the upper/lower strip KMS boundary convention. Hiai writes the modular convention at width beta = -1; the local lemma uses the upper-strip convention of its exact supplier.

references.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1311.2717
references.locator: Complete 157-page lecture notes; §3.4, Definition 3.4.4 (printed pp. 74–75, PDF pp. 73–74), for the C*-dynamical KMS strip with physical width hbar beta. That definition assumes a strongly continuous C*-flow; the present W*-rescaling is proved directly and does not use that hypothesis.

items.title: Free scalar wedge data and modular-geometric bridge
items.physical_scope: One selected massive, noninteracting real scalar vacuum representation on four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime, its right-wedge local Weyl algebra, and the assumed modular/boost bridge. This scope includes neither a detector model nor an empirical temperature measurement, an interacting QFT, or a general curved-spacetime result.
items.statement:
Assume both the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice. Fix a
massive real scalar species with rest mass $m_{\mathrm{rest}}>0$ in kilograms.
Use four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime with metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and length coordinates
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, where $x^0=ct$ and $c>0$ has units
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Set $\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest}}c/\hbar>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, where $\hbar>0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. The future shell,
one-particle space, and measure are
$$H_\mu^+=\{(p^0,\mathbf p):(p^0)^2-|\mathbf p|^2=\mu^2,\ p^0>0\},\qquad \mathcal H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu),\qquad d\nu_\mu=\frac{d^3\mathbf p}{(2\pi)^3\,2\sqrt{|\mathbf p|^2+\mu^2}}.$$
Take the scalar Hilbert space to be the bosonic symmetric Fock space
$\mathcal H=\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_\mu)$ and its unit zero-particle vector
to be $\Omega$.

For an open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ and real
$f\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb R)$, define
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x, \qquad W_\mu(f)=W_{\mathrm{Segal}}(\sqrt2\,K_\mu f).$$
Let $\mathfrak A_s(O)$ be the operator-norm closure of the unital
$*$-algebra generated by all these bounded Weyl unitaries, and set
$W_R=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:x^1>|x^0|\}$ and
$M(W_R)=\mathfrak A_s(W_R)''\subseteq\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Here
$\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ denotes the bounded linear operators;
$\mathcal S'$ is the set of bounded operators commuting with every member of
$\mathcal S$, and $\mathcal S''=(\mathcal S')'$. Thus $M(W_R)$ is a concrete
von Neumann algebra in the chosen double-commutant convention.

For dimensionless rapidity $s\in\mathbb R$, define the future-directed boost
by
$$\Lambda_W(s)(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) =(x^0\cosh s+x^1\sinh s,\ x^0\sinh s+x^1\cosh s,\ x^2,\ x^3).$$
Use its scalar Fock implementation: on the one-particle space
$[u_\mu(\Lambda)\psi](p)=\psi(\Lambda^{-1}p)$, and on the $n$-particle
symmetric sector $U(\Lambda)=u_\mu(\Lambda)^{\otimes_s n}$, with the vacuum
sector fixed. The QFT Fock pairing is linear in its second argument; for the
modular definitions use the equivalent first-variable-linear pairing
$\langle u,v\rangle_1:=\langle v,u\rangle_2$. Thus the vacuum vector state
is $\omega_W(X)=\langle X\Omega,\Omega\rangle_1
=\langle\Omega,X\Omega\rangle_2$. Assume explicitly that $\Omega$ is cyclic and separating for
$M(W_R)$, meaning $\overline{M(W_R)\Omega}=\mathcal H$ and
$X\Omega=0$ for $X\in M(W_R)$ implies $X=0$. The Tomita operator is the
closure of $S_{W,0}(X\Omega)=X^*\Omega$ on $M(W_R)\Omega$; write its polar
decomposition as $S_W=J_W\Delta_W^{1/2}$, in the standard modular-data
convention.

As an additional model interface, adopt
$$\Delta_W^{it}=U(\Lambda_W(-2\pi t))\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
This geometric identity and cyclic-separating property are explicit adopted
assumptions for this selected model. The abstract Tomita–Takesaki theorem
supplies modular automorphisms and their KMS property, but this carrier does
not use it as a proof that the modular unitaries equal spacetime boosts. No
tensor-product factorization of the continuum Hilbert space across the wedge
and its complement is assumed.

references.title: Joseph J. Bisognano and Eyvind H. Wichmann, On the duality condition for a Hermitian scalar field, Journal of Mathematical Physics 16 (1975), 985–1007
references.locator: Complete 24-page PDF; §II (PDF pp. 2–5), §IV and Theorem 1 (pp. 7–10), and §V (pp. 10–15). The source proves analytic wedge relations under its Wightman assumptions; the carrier adopts the stated bridge as a model input and does not import those assumptions implicitly.

references.title: Daniele Guido, Modular theory for the von Neumann algebras of local quantum physics, complete lecture notes, arXiv:0812.1511
references.locator: Complete 28-page PDF; §2.1 (PDF pp. 2–10) on the free scalar one-particle/Fock construction; §§3.1.1–3.1.2 (pp. 14–17) on the one-particle and Wightman Bisognano–Wichmann relations; §3.3 (p. 20) on KMS interpretation. The note uses its own (+---) metric and boost parameter; the local statement fixes the sign explicitly.

references.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1803.04993
references.locator: Complete 80-page PDF; §§5.3–5.4 (PDF pp. 53–56), the Bisognano–Wichmann holomorphy sketch and accelerated orbit. The author explicitly calls the preceding path-integral/factorization account nonrigorous; this source is used for convention and interpretation context, not as the local proof.

references.title: Stefan Hollands and Robert M. Wald, Quantum fields in curved spacetime, arXiv:1401.2026
references.locator: Complete 77-page review; §2.2(a), PDF pp. 20–22, Rindler wedge, boost-time KMS state and the distinction between the algebraic state and detector interpretation. The displayed two-point example sets the mass to zero; it is context, not a premise for the selected massive model.

references.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, arXiv:gr-qc/9912119
references.locator: Complete 46-page review; §3, printed pp. 11–16 (PDF pp. 12–16), distinguishing Unruh and Hawking states and the boost/KMS interpretation. The review uses natural units; no Hawking or black-hole claim is imported here.

items.title: Wedge modular bridge implies the Unruh clock temperature
items.physical_scope: An algebraic KMS statement for the vacuum state of the selected massive scalar right-wedge model, conditional on its adopted modular/boost bridge, and for one uniformly accelerated proper-time orbit. It asserts no detector response, particle production, observed temperature, Hawking effect, or density-matrix representation.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the selected massive scalar wedge postulate.
Use its metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, length coordinates
$x^0=ct$, right wedge $W_R=\{x^1>|x^0|\}$, vacuum $\Omega$, algebra
$M=M(W_R)$, modular operator $\Delta_W$, first-variable-linear pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_1$ from the postulate, and boost
$\Lambda_W(s)$ with
dimensionless rapidity $s$. Define the vector state
$\omega_W(X)=\langle X\Omega,\Omega\rangle_1$ for $X\in M$, the modular
automorphisms $\sigma_t(X)=\Delta_W^{it}X\Delta_W^{-it}$, and
$\alpha_t=\sigma_{-t}$ for dimensionless $t$. The proper-time curve for
any $a>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ is
$$\gamma_a(\tau)=\left(\frac{c^2}{a}\sinh\frac{a\tau}{c}, \frac{c^2}{a}\cosh\frac{a\tau}{c},0,0\right),\qquad \tau\in\mathbb R,$$
where $\tau$ is measured in seconds. Its future-boost rapidity is
$s=a\tau/c$. For this unit proper-time parametrization, define the
proper-acceleration scalar by
$a_\gamma=\sqrt{\eta(\ddot\gamma_a,\ddot\gamma_a)}$; the theorem verifies
$a_\gamma=a$. Define the proper-time action on $M$ by
$\widetilde\alpha_\tau=\alpha_{a\tau/(2\pi c)}$; equivalently, it is
conjugation by the future boost $U(\Lambda_W(a\tau/c))$.

Then for every $A,B\in M$ there is a bounded function $G_{A,B}$, continuous
on the closed strip $0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b_U$ and holomorphic inside,
whose boundaries satisfy
$$G_{A,B}(\tau)=\omega_W(A\widetilde\alpha_\tau(B)),\qquad G_{A,B}(\tau+i b_U)=\omega_W(\widetilde\alpha_\tau(B)A) \quad(\tau\in\mathbb R),$$
with strip width $b_U=2\pi c/a$ seconds. Under the physical-time convention
that the strip width is $\hbar\beta_U$, the associated inverse temperature
and KMS temperature parameter are
$$\beta_U=\frac{2\pi c}{a\hbar},\qquad T_U=\frac{1}{k_B\beta_U}=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B},$$
where $\hbar>0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $k_B>0$ is in
$\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. This is a conditional algebraic model deduction; it
does not assert a detector response, particle production, a thermal
density matrix, or an observed temperature.

references.title: Joseph J. Bisognano and Eyvind H. Wichmann, On the duality condition for a Hermitian scalar field, Journal of Mathematical Physics 16 (1975), 985–1007
references.locator: Complete 24-page PDF; §IV and Theorem 1 (PDF pp. 7–10) give the analytic wedge relation under the paper's field hypotheses. The current result instead derives the clock conversion conditionally from the explicitly adopted bridge.

references.title: Daniele Guido, Modular theory for the von Neumann algebras of local quantum physics, complete lecture notes, arXiv:0812.1511
references.locator: Complete 28-page PDF; §§3.1.1–3.1.2 (PDF pp. 14–17) state the free scalar and Wightman Bisognano–Wichmann relations; §3.3 (p. 20) interprets the boost KMS strip as the accelerated-observer temperature. Its boost convention is translated to the stated future-boost sign.

references.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1803.04993
references.locator: Complete 80-page PDF; §5.3 (PDF pp. 53–54) sketches the Bisognano–Wichmann holomorphy argument and §5.4 (pp. 54–56) derives the accelerated-orbit strip width. The notes state that their path-integral factorization route is not rigorous; the present proof does not rely on that route or on Witten's sketch.

references.title: Stefan Hollands and Robert M. Wald, Quantum fields in curved spacetime, arXiv:1401.2026
references.locator: Complete 77-page review; §2.2(a), PDF pp. 20–22, states the Rindler-algebra KMS result and explains the boost-time/acceleration interpretation. Its massless two-point example and detector discussion are not used as premises.

references.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, arXiv:gr-qc/9912119
references.locator: Complete 46-page review; §3, printed pp. 11–16 (PDF pp. 12–16), states the Unruh KMS temperature and explicitly distinguishes the Unruh and Hawking states. The source sets c and hbar to one; the SI conversion is proved locally.

title: Free scalar wedge modular geometry — Examples

items.title: Finite two-mode squeeze illustrates but does not construct wedge factorization
items.physical_scope: A two-oscillator-mode illustration of a reduced state and its entropy. It is not a construction of the continuum wedge algebra's inside/outside factorization, a thermal density matrix for that algebra, or an experimental observation.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H_R=\mathcal H_L=\ell^2(\mathbb N_0)$ with orthonormal number
bases $\{|n\rangle_R:n\in\mathbb N_0\}$ and
$\{|n\rangle_L:n\in\mathbb N_0\}$. Use inner products linear in the second
variable. For a Hilbert space $K$, write $\mathcal B(K)$ for its bounded
linear operators, and for $u,v\in K$ write $|u\rangle\langle v|$ for the
rank-one operator $w\mapsto u\langle v,w\rangle$. For dimensionless
$0<z<1$, define
$$|\psi_z\rangle=\sqrt{1-z}\sum_{n=0}^\infty z^{n/2} |n\rangle_R\otimes|n\rangle_L.$$
Define its left-traced operator $\rho_R$ by
$$\langle m|\rho_R|n\rangle =\sum_{k=0}^\infty \langle m,k|\psi_z\rangle\overline{\langle n,k|\psi_z\rangle}.$$
This coefficient formula defines the partial trace of this rank-one operator
over the left oscillator. The vector is normalized, and $\rho_R$ is a
positive diagonal operator with eigenvalues $p_n=(1-z)z^n$, whose sum is one.
Its entropy in nats, using the natural logarithm, is
$$S(\rho_R)=-\sum_{n=0}^\infty p_n\ln p_n =-\ln(1-z)-\frac{z\ln z}{1-z}.$$
This explicitly constructed pair of oscillator modes does not construct a
tensor-product factorization of the continuum right-wedge Hilbert space or a
density matrix for its local von Neumann algebra.

references.title: Daniel Harlow, Jerusalem Lectures on Black Holes and Quantum Information, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1409.1231
references.locator: Complete lecture notes; §3.2–3.3 (PDF pp. 15–21), the finite-system entanglement analogy, Rindler decomposition, and the limitations of a naive continuum tensor-factor picture. The oscillator normalization, partial trace, and entropy are derived locally below.

references.title: Edward Witten, Notes on Some Entanglement Properties of Quantum Field Theory, complete lecture notes, arXiv:1803.04993
references.locator: Complete 80-page lecture notes inspected at §§5.2–5.3 (PDF pp. 47–54). Section 5.2 explicitly qualifies the Euclidean path-integral/factorization account as nonrigorous; this supports the example's continuum-scope warning, not its oscillator calculations.
